subject: principles-of-accounts
introduction: Key equations, ledger rules, and ratios for CSEC Principles of Accounts — from double entry to financial-statement analysis.

items.name: Accounting equation
items.formula: Assets = Capital + Liabilities
items.notes: So Capital = Assets − Liabilities. Every transaction keeps the equation balanced.

items.name: Business entity concept
items.formula: the business is separate from its owner
items.notes: Owner's personal items are never business assets; drawings reduce capital.

items.name: Going concern / prudence / accruals
items.formula: assume continuity; anticipate no profits but all losses; match income/costs to the period
items.notes: Historic cost: record assets at original cost.

items.name: Double-entry rule
items.formula: every transaction: equal debit and credit
items.notes: Debits: increase assets/expenses, decrease liabilities/income/capital. Credits: the reverse.

sections.title: Books of original entry and the ledger

items.name: Sales journal / purchases journal
items.formula: record CREDIT sales / CREDIT purchases
items.notes: Cash sales/purchases go straight to the cash book, not the journals.

items.name: Returns
items.formula: sales returns → sales returns journal (credit note issued); purchases returns → debit note issued
items.notes: Carriage inwards (on purchases) is an expense added to cost of sales; carriage outwards (on sales) is a selling expense.

items.name: Cash book / petty cash
items.formula: cash book is both book of entry and ledger; petty cash uses the imprest system
items.notes: Contra entry: cash banked or withdrawn (Dr and Cr in the cash book at once).

items.name: Trial balance purpose
items.formula: checks arithmetical accuracy of double entry
items.notes: It does NOT catch errors of omission, commission, principle, original entry, reversal, or compensation.

items.name: Suspense account
items.formula: temporary account for the trial-balance difference
items.notes: Opened when debits ≠ credits; cleared when errors are corrected.

items.name: Cost of sales
items.formula: opening stock + purchases (+ carriage inwards) − closing stock
items.notes: Closing stock valued at lower of cost and net realizable value.

items.name: Gross profit
items.formula: gross profit = sales − cost of sales
items.notes: Gross profit % = (gross profit / sales) × 100.

items.name: Net profit
items.formula: net profit = gross profit − expenses + other income
items.notes: Net margin = (net profit / sales) × 100. Net profit is added to capital.

items.name: Statement of financial position
items.formula: Assets = Capital + Liabilities at a date
items.notes: Order: non-current assets, current assets; capital; non-current then current liabilities.

items.name: Working capital
items.formula: working capital = current assets − current liabilities
items.notes: Capital employed = non-current liabilities + equity (or total assets − current liabilities).

items.name: Depreciation (straight line)
items.formula: annual = (cost − residual value) / useful life
items.notes: Reducing balance: fixed % of net book value each year. Depreciation is a non-cash expense.

items.name: Bad debts / provisions
items.formula: bad debt written off: Dr Bad debts, Cr Debtor; provision for doubtful debts = estimated % of receivables
items.notes: Accrued expense (owing) = current liability; prepayment (paid in advance) = current asset.

sections.title: Ratios, control accounts and business forms

items.name: Current ratio
items.formula: current assets / current liabilities (ideal ≈ 2:1)
items.notes: Acid test (quick) ratio = (current assets − stock) / current liabilities (≈ 1:1).

items.name: Profitability ratios
items.formula: ROCE = (net profit / capital employed) × 100
items.notes: Higher gross/net margins and ROCE = better performance.

items.name: Bank reconciliation
items.formula: updated cash book = bank statement ± timing differences
items.notes: Unpresented cheques and uncleared deposits explain most differences.

items.name: Receivables / payables control
items.formula: summarise total debtors / creditors ledgers
items.notes: Cash received from customers credited in the receivables control.

items.name: Partnerships vs companies
items.formula: partnership: 2–20 owners, profit per agreement; company: owned by shareholders, capital in shares
items.notes: Partnership interest on capital is an appropriation of profit, not an expense.
